The least-significant digit of \(N\) in base \(T\) is \(d = N \bmod T = 54443359375 = 223 \times 15625^2\). Thus the back-door relation holds for \(k = 223\) and the residue \(s = 15625\), so one may write
\[
q = bT + s,\qquad p = aT + ks
\]
with unknown positive integers \(a,b\). Substituting into \(pq = N\) produces the Diophantine equation
\[
ab\cdot T + s(a + kb) = Q,
\]
where \(Q = \lfloor N/T\rfloor = 91743180694441165498\). The unique solution in the feasible range \(a,b\approx 50\) is \(a=54\), \(b=52\). Consequently
\[
q = 52\cdot T + 15625 = 1698947790634444037.
\]
(The complementary factor is larger, both factors have exactly 61 bits, and their product equals \(N\).)
